title: Variation: Human Centric School Lighting

findings.antecedent: manual control of light settings by teachers
findings.consequent: teachers leaving one light setting in position for a long time
findings.mechanism: Teachers tend to leave one light setting on, leading to prolonged exposure to potentially unsuitable light.
findings.quote: when one light setting has been turned on the teachers tend to leave it in that position.

findings.antecedent: activating light (high intensity, blue-enriched) on during a large part of the day
findings.consequent: headaches in some pupils
findings.mechanism: Prolonged exposure to activating light may cause discomfort or physiological stress in some individuals.
findings.quote: it is unsuitable to have the activating light on during a large part of the day, because then some pupils tend to get a headache.

findings.antecedent: old fluorescent tube lighting in classroom
findings.consequent: light perceived as harsh
findings.quote: The principal teacher describes the light as harsh.

findings.antecedent: placement of inner light switch in classroom
findings.consequent: difficulty for teachers to reach
findings.quote: The teachers describe the inner light switch as hard to reach.

findings.antecedent: smart board on with room light on
findings.consequent: difficulty for pupils to see what they write
findings.mechanism: Glare from the smart board makes it difficult to see written material.
findings.quote: When the smart board is on, the light must be turned off causing difficulties for the pupils to see what they write.

findings.consequent: classroom atmosphere (messier)
findings.quote: Morning lessons are often calm, messier before lunch and after lunch.

findings.consequent: pupils becoming messy, noisy, and unfocused
findings.mechanism: Fatigue affects pupils' self-regulation and attention.
findings.quote: Some pupils become messy and noisy and unfocused when they are tired (either due to lack of sleep or lack of energy).

findings.consequent: pupils' feelings, well-being, and ability to work
findings.quote: 87 % of the pupils responded that the lighting is important for how they feel/ are able to work in a room.

findings.antecedent: sudden changes in light intensity and color temperature (automatic light variation)
findings.consequent: distraction in pupils
findings.mechanism: Abrupt changes in the visual environment can disrupt attention.
findings.quote: 9/23 pupils spontaneously expressed that the sudden changes were distracting.

findings.antecedent: returning to classroom after breaks (after daylight exposure, then yellowish corridor light)
findings.consequent: headaches in one pupil with migraine
findings.mechanism: Sharp transitions between different light environments may trigger headaches in sensitive individuals.
findings.quote: One pupil (with migraine) thinks that the light is working all right when he comes to school, but he gets a headache when he gets back to the classroom after the breaks.

findings.consequent: disturbing feeling and headaches in some pupils
findings.mechanism: High intensity blue light may cause discomfort or physiological stress in sensitive individuals.
findings.quote: A few of the pupils experience the activating light as disturbing, one example: “Intense blue light gives me a headache”

findings.consequent: perceived as bluish by pupils
findings.quote: The 6500 K light, the ”activating light”, is perceived as blue by the majority of the pupils.

findings.consequent: perceived as reddish by pupils
findings.quote: The 2700 K light, the “calming light” is perceived as quite reddish

findings.consequent: perceived as soft by pupils
findings.quote: The red light is perceived as soft by a majority of the pupils.

findings.consequent: perceived as comfortable by pupils
findings.quote: A slightly larger proportion of the pupils perceive the red light as comfortable.

findings.consequent: perceived as disturbing by pupils
findings.quote: Some of the pupils perceive the blue light as comfortable, some perceive it as disturbing.

findings.consequent: perceived as tiring by pupils
findings.quote: Red light is perceived as tiring by a majority of the pupils.

findings.consequent: perceived as stimulating by pupils
findings.quote: Blue light is perceived neither as tiring, nor as activating.

findings.consequent: perceived as unpleasant by pupils
findings.quote: Some of the pupils prefer the blue light, some of them prefer the red light.

findings.consequent: perceived as pleasant by pupils
findings.quote: Some of the pupils prefer the blue light, some of them prefer the red light.

findings.consequent: pupils' preference for concentration
findings.mechanism: Most pupils prefer a light color between red and blue for concentration.
findings.quote: Most of the pupils say that they prefer a color of the light that is between the red and the blue.

findings.consequent: pupil satisfaction, comfort, concentration, alertness, perception of flickering, coolness
findings.quote: 5/5 pupils are satisfied with the light installation: “I think the light is a bit more comfortable, you concentrate better.”

findings.consequent: pupil satisfaction
findings.quote: 5/5 pupils say that it is good that there is a possibility to vary the color of the light: “It's good because then you can choose the brightness you want after how you feel”

findings.consequent: pupil preference for daylight or daylight-like light
findings.quote: 5/5 pupils prefer daylight or daylight like light: “The best is when there is no (artificial) light at all and that the light is coming from the windows.

findings.consequent: pupil preference for intermediate color
findings.quote: 4/5 pupils would like the color of the light to be somewhere in between the orange and the blue

findings.consequent: pupil appreciation
findings.mechanism: The Smartboard mode allows visibility of the screen while also enabling reading/writing at benches.
findings.quote: 5/5 pupils appreciate “Smartboard”: “When we are using the Smartboard now, there is no need to turn off lights, but just switch to Smartboard position.”

findings.consequent: pupil liking
findings.quote: 5/5 pupils like the new luminaires: “They are cool”, “They look nice”

findings.consequent: flickering perceived by pupils
findings.quote: 2/5 pupils say that the old luminaires where flickering: “I just feel that they don’t blink like these (the old lighting in the classroom where we are sitting) because sometimes they blink and it’s disturbing.

findings.consequent: increased headaches in one pupil
findings.mechanism: The new lighting, particularly blue light, triggered daily headaches in a sensitive pupil.
findings.quote: 1/5 pupils experienced more headaches after the installation: “I thought it was fun when we got it but then I noticed that I got a headache almost every day, in school.

findings.consequent: risk of headache and preference for darker, reddish-yellow light
findings.quote: Strong light induces the risk of headache: ”I prefer darker light. Rather the reddish-yellow, than the blue.”

findings.consequent: pupil alertness and tiredness
findings.mechanism: Intense light is associated with alertness, while comfortable light is associated with tiredness.
findings.quote: “When the light is intense you become alert. When the light feels comfortable you get very tired.”

findings.antecedent: light change start-up time (2 minutes for Dialogue mode)
findings.consequent: pupil preference for longer start-up time
findings.mechanism: Pupils prefer gradual, less noticeable transitions in lighting.
findings.quote: 6/23 pupils would prefer a longer start up time than 2 minutes

findings.antecedent: light change start-up time (2 minutes for Dialogue mode)
findings.consequent: pupil preference for more rapid start-up time
findings.quote: only one pupil would prefer a more rapid start up.

findings.consequent: room feeling comfortable, calm, not stimulating, and gloomy due to low light level
findings.mechanism: The low light level, despite being comfortable, contributes to a gloomy and non-stimulating atmosphere.
findings.quote: The luminance level in the room feels comfortable and calm with just enough light. ... It does not feel stimulating as the activating light, in an awakening sense. In a way the room looks fairly gloomy, probably due to the low light level.

findings.consequent: human faces looking most alive, red curtains looking nice, feeling more stimulating than neutral light, light color matching interior parts
findings.mechanism: Warmer light with higher intensity enhances visual perception of faces and interior colors, contributing to a more stimulating and natural appearance.
findings.quote: This is the light setting that makes the human faces look most alive and the red curtains are also nice in this light. In my own opinion this light feels more stimulating than the neutral light, probably because the light level is about 40 % higher. The light color seems to match many interior parts

findings.consequent: luminaire surfaces looking strange, reddish tone, somewhat unnatural
findings.mechanism: The warm color temperature on the luminaire surface might create an unusual visual impression, like reddish clouds.
findings.quote: The luminaire surfaces looks a bit strange in this light, like if there was a cloudy day above but with a somewhat reddish tone as if the clouds were a little bit red. This feels somewhat unnatural.

findings.consequent: room feeling bright and stimulating, everything looking cleaner, upper wall luminous
findings.mechanism: High intensity, cold white light enhances brightness and a sense of cleanliness, contributing to a stimulating atmosphere.
findings.quote: This light atmosphere is bright and feels stimulating. In a way everything looks a bit cleaner, for example the upper part of the upper wall looks clearly white, almost a bit luminous.

findings.consequent: atmosphere feeling unnatural, greyish, influencing human face color, wooden/table surfaces looking orange/brownish
findings.mechanism: The cold color temperature distorts natural colors, making faces appear greyish and warm-toned surfaces appear brownish.
findings.quote: But on the other hand the atmosphere feels a bit unnatural, a bit greyish, which also influence the color of human faces. The wooden parts and the table surfaces are rather orange and they look rather brownish in the activating light.

findings.consequent: luminaire surfaces looking like blue sky through clouds, unnatural
findings.mechanism: The bright, bluish luminaire surfaces create an unusual and somewhat artificial visual impression.
findings.quote: The bright luminaire surfaces look like something in between a blue sky and a sky with thin white clouds. Thinking critically about the color it looks as if it was light from a blue sky coming in through clouds, which feels a bit unnatural.

findings.consequent: diffuse, even light distribution with hardly any shadows
findings.mechanism: Large luminous surfaces inherently produce diffuse light, minimizing sharp shadows.
findings.quote: This luminaire has a quite large luminous surface, 60 × 60 cm, which generates a diffuse, even light distribution and in this kind of environment there are shadows with diffuse borders

findings.consequent: somewhat lifeless atmosphere, lack of dramatic ingredient, mimics of faces hardly visualised
findings.mechanism: Lack of contrast and variation in light can reduce visual interest and expressiveness.
findings.quote: In my opinion the evenness create a somewhat lifeless atmosphere in the room and it would be a good idea to add different layers of light, e.g. with spotlights. There is hardly any dramatic ingredient in the light and the mimics of the faces is hardly visualised.

findings.antecedent: large luminous surfaces of new luminaires
findings.consequent: low risk of glare
findings.mechanism: Larger light sources distribute light more broadly, reducing concentrated brightness that causes glare.
findings.quote: The large luminous surfaces minimize the risk of glare and looking at a computer screen or a white A4 paper there is no disturbing glare.

findings.consequent: visibility slightly better with hand blocking light (for 60-year old participant)
findings.mechanism: Even low glare can be noticeable to sensitive individuals or older eyes.
findings.quote: in the Neutral character the visibility was a bit better with the hand blocking the light.

findings.consequent: less glary than Neutral character (4000 K) (for 60-year old participant)
findings.mechanism: Warmer light may be perceived as less harsh or glary.
findings.quote: the Dialogue character was a bit less glary than the Neutral character.

findings.consequent: more glare than Neutral (4000 K) and Dialogue (2700 K) characters (for 60-year old participant)
findings.mechanism: Colder, higher intensity light can increase perceived glare.
findings.quote: The simple glare test with the 60-year old revealed more glare than for the Neutral and Dialogue characters.

findings.consequent: light from luminaire seeming white with a very light, red tone
findings.quote: The light from the luminaire seem white with a very light, red tone.

findings.consequent: light from luminaire perceived as warm white with a reddish tone
findings.quote: The impression of the light from the luminaire is warm white with a reddish tone.

findings.consequent: light from luminaire perceived as cold white with a bluish tone, a bit unnatural
findings.quote: The impression of the light from the luminaire is cold white with a bluish tone, a bit unnatural.

findings.consequent: red, green, and blue colors seeming equally prominent
findings.mechanism: White light generally provides versatile color rendering.
findings.quote: My impression is that red, green and blue colors seem just as prominent under this light

findings.consequent: flattering for skin, red colors more prominent, blue colors darker
findings.mechanism: The prominence of red wavelengths in warmer light enhances red tones and skin appearance, while making blue tones recede.
findings.quote: The yellow light in the dialogue mode is a flattering one for the skin. ... The red colors in the room seem a bit more prominent and blue colors seem darker

findings.consequent: facial color seeming grey/blue/purple, green and blue colors seeming more prominent
findings.mechanism: Blue-enriched light can alter the perception of skin tones and enhance blue/green colors.
findings.quote: The facial color seems somewhat grey/blue/purple in the activating mode. Green and blue colors seem a bit more prominent

findings.consequent: red colors seeming more vivid
findings.quote: The red colors in the dialogue light seem more vivid.

findings.consequent: red colors becoming darker and less prominent
findings.quote: The red colors in the activating light becomes darker and not as prominent.

findings.consequent: teacher satisfaction and interest in light variation
findings.quote: Overall the teachers are very positive to the new lighting and the possibility to vary the light

findings.consequent: problematic for 20% of pupils (hypersensitive)
findings.mechanism: Intense light may cause discomfort or adverse reactions in sensitive individuals.
findings.quote: One of the teachers says that the focus light may be a problem for 20 % (the hypersensitive ones) of the pupils.

findings.consequent: most pupils seeming more focused and less tired
findings.quote: Most of the other pupils seem more focused and less tired now.

findings.consequent: normal pupils complaining less about headaches
findings.quote: The “normal pupils” complain less about headaches than before.

findings.consequent: teachers feeling less tired and having fewer headaches
findings.quote: The teachers themselves feel less tired and have fever headaches now.

findings.consequent: teachers never switching light mode without preparing pupils
findings.mechanism: Teachers use light changes as a pedagogical cue, requiring prior communication.
findings.quote: The teachers never switch the light mode without preparing the pupils.

findings.consequent: used as a pedagogic tool by one teacher
findings.mechanism: The distinct character of focus light makes it suitable for signaling concentration periods.
findings.quote: One of the teachers use focus light as a pedagogic tool: “Now it’s time to concentrate!”.

findings.consequent: pupil preference for slower variations
findings.mechanism: Gradual changes are less distracting and more comfortable.
findings.quote: Most pupils would prefer slower variations than the two minutes slopes that have been operating during most of the tests.

findings.consequent: appreciation by most pupils
findings.quote: The activating light is appreciated by most.

findings.consequent: perceived as very intense by several pupils
findings.quote: However, several pupils have written, said and shown that they feel that the activating light is very intense.

findings.consequent: increased headaches in 1-2 pupils (more with Awakening light)
findings.mechanism: Specific light characters, particularly blue-enriched awakening light, triggered headaches in sensitive individuals.
findings.quote: one or two of the 23 pupils in Malmö, had an increased rate of headaches. Those pupils had earlier problems with migraine and the symptoms occurred in the Dialogue as well as the Awakening light, with a somewhat higher occurrence in the Awakening light.

findings.consequent: positive perception by majority of pupils and teachers
findings.quote: The majority of the group, pupils as well as the teachers are very positive to the new lighting and the possibility to vary the light.

findings.antecedent: sudden changes in intensity and/or color temperature (automatic variation or between rooms)
findings.consequent: disturbing feeling and higher risk for headaches
findings.mechanism: Abrupt light changes can be visually disruptive and physiologically stressful, especially for sensitive individuals.
findings.quote: sudden changes in intensity and/or color temperature, within the automatic variation in the room and through movements between rooms with very different light characteristics, was disturbing and also induced a higher risk for headaches.

findings.consequent: more intense and better color rendition compared to Malmö
findings.quote: My own perception is that the Activating light is more intense at the Kongsgårdmoen school than it is in Malmö, which is consistent with the values presented above. The activating light at Kongsgårdmoen seems to give a better color rendition than the activating light in Malmö

findings.antecedent: wall, ceiling, and floor colors at Kongsgårdmoen school
findings.consequent: adapted to higher color temperature, use of blue and white
findings.mechanism: Interior design choices complement the desired light characteristics.
findings.quote: The choices of wall, ceiling and floor colors seems to be adapted to a higher color temperature. Kongsgårdmoen use a lot of blue and white which is represented well in a higher color temperature.

findings.consequent: new, beige, positive impression in activating light
findings.quote: The wooden details are also new, fairly beige and I had a positive impression of this also in the activating light.

findings.antecedent: Dialogue light at Malmö school (matching furniture)
findings.consequent: feeling more comfortable compared to Kongsgårdmoen
findings.mechanism: Visual harmony between lighting and interior elements enhances comfort.
findings.quote: This light feels more comfortable in Malmö, probably because it matches the furniture.

findings.antecedent: Dialogue light at Kongsgårdmoen school (activating light perceived as intense)
findings.consequent: more appreciated by pupils
findings.mechanism: The contrast with a very intense activating light might make the dialogue light feel more pleasant by comparison.
findings.quote: However the Dialogue light seems to be more appreciated in Kongsgårdmoen, possibly because their activating light is perceived to be so intense.

findings.consequent: pupils' feelings, well-being, and ability to work
findings.quote: 90 % of the 20 pupils responded that the lighting is important for how they feel/ are able to work in a room.

findings.consequent: pupil appreciation
findings.quote: Most of the pupils appreciate the new light.

findings.consequent: pupils perceiving changes as sudden
findings.mechanism: Rapid transitions are easily noticeable and can be perceived as abrupt.
findings.quote: Most of the pupils perceive the changes as sudden

findings.consequent: pupil desire to decrease speed
findings.mechanism: Pupils prefer gradual, less noticeable transitions in lighting.
findings.quote: Most of the pupils (14/20) would enjoy decrease the speed of the changes.

findings.consequent: pupil desire to decrease intensity
findings.mechanism: High intensity light can be perceived as uncomfortable or too strong.
findings.quote: A majority of the pupils would like to decrease the intensity of the focus light

findings.consequent: pupil perception of it being too intense
findings.quote: A majority of the pupils perceive the activating light as too intense.

findings.consequent: pupil perception of it being bluish
findings.quote: A majority of the pupils perceive the activating light as bluish.

findings.consequent: pupil perception of it being intense or quite intense
findings.quote: Most of the pupils perceive the activating light as intense or quite intense.

findings.consequent: pupil perception of it being quite disturbing
findings.quote: A majority of the pupils perceive the activating light as quite disturbing.

findings.consequent: pupil perception of it being tiring
findings.quote: The pupils’ opinions are divided regarding whether the activating light is stimulating or tiring.

findings.consequent: pupil perception of it being unpleasant
findings.quote: The activating light is not perceived as unpleasant nor pleasant.

findings.consequent: pupils reporting eye pain and headache
findings.mechanism: Intense activating light can cause physical discomfort in some pupils.
findings.quote: 4/20 pupils expresses spontaneously that they don’t like the activating light: ”My eyes hurt from the focus light.”

findings.consequent: pupil appreciation
findings.quote: 3/20 pupils spontaneously express they appreciate the natural light: ”Sunset is good.”, ”I think daylight is the best.”

findings.consequent: pupil preference
findings.quote: 7/20 pupils say that they would like green or water-colored light

findings.consequent: pupil preference
findings.quote: 11/20 of the pupils prefer “neutral light” or “dialogue light”

findings.antecedent: focus light or neutral light for theoretical tasks
findings.consequent: pupil suggestion for use
findings.mechanism: Specific light settings are perceived as more suitable for certain cognitive tasks.
findings.quote: 7/20 suggest focus light or neutral light for theoretical tasks

findings.consequent: pupil suggestion for use
findings.mechanism: Specific light settings are perceived as more suitable for certain social tasks.
findings.quote: and dialogue light for cooperation tasks

findings.consequent: pupils reporting hurting eyes or head
findings.mechanism: Intense focus light can cause physical discomfort in some pupils.
findings.quote: 3 pupils were talking about hurting eyes or head, one said it’s annoying when the focus light is turned on.

findings.consequent: teachers finding it difficult to talk about them
findings.mechanism: Lack of a common language or clear understanding of new lighting properties makes communication challenging.
findings.quote: The interviewed teachers say that they find it a bit difficult to know how to talk about the new lighting which is a clear argument for why the new concepts, the lighting characters, are so needed.

findings.consequent: at least two teachers using it as a pedagogical tool
findings.mechanism: The ability to change light settings allows teachers to visually signal transitions or focus periods.
findings.quote: the interviews at Kongsgårdmoen show that at least two teachers are using the manual control possibility as a pedagogical tool

findings.consequent: appreciated by pupils and teachers for looking like ceiling windows
findings.mechanism: The visual appearance of the luminaires mimics natural light sources, which is positively perceived.
findings.quote: The 60 × 60 plates are appreciated because they look like ceiling windows.

findings.consequent: pupils and teachers showing great interest
findings.quote: Teachers as well as pupils have shown great interest in the light installations.

findings.consequent: perceived as a positive example for indoor lighting by pupils and teachers
findings.quote: Numerous comments from both pupils and teachers indicate that they perceive the natural daylight as a positive example for how the indoor lighting ought to be.

stimuli.description: Classroom in Malmö with new Candelux 60x60 LED panels, dimmable (3000K-6000K, CRI 85, 3800 lm), controlled by DALI/Crestron system. Lighting characters included 'Activating' (700 lux, 6500 K), 'Calming' (350 lux, 2700 K), 'Smartboard' (dimmed front).

Classroom in Kongsgårdmoen school with recessed Modul R 600 LED Premium luminaires (Ra: > 90), tuneable white. Settings included 'Morning' (650 lux, 6500 K), 'Awakening' (1000 lux, 6500 K), 'Neutral' (300 lux, 3500 K), 'Restful' (300 lux, 2700 K).

limitations: The installation of the automatic light variation was more complicated and took longer than expected.
The study did not intend to make extensive observations and measurements beyond the primary focus.
The spatial distribution of light was hardly assessed in this thesis.
No daylight-related control of the lighting level was included in the design or installation for practical and economic reasons.
This thesis does not aim to contribute to the basic scientific knowledge on how non-visual effects influence circadian cycles.
The study did not include new furniture, plants, etc., which could enhance the effect of lighting.

The study does not intend to prove how this particular light affects pupils' health, well-being, and performance, acknowledging other influencing factors like visual connections to the yard, noise, air quality, and social relations.
The installation of luminaires and initial controls was subject to continuous improvements, indicating ongoing technical challenges.
A large rapid (400 Hz) and irregular variation was noticed on the oscilloscope screen during flicker measurements, which is an important area for further research.
There was a significant dip in illuminance during the first minute of light character start-up, which is assumed to be a technical problem.
